description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Uganda Country Programme works to reduce trade costs, strengthen regional connectivity, and build a more competitive and inclusive trading economy, operating along the Northern Corridor since 2011 in alignment with Uganda's Vision 2040, NDP IV, and AfCFTA and EAC integration commitments. The Programme has delivered a comprehensive portfolio of physical and digital trade infrastructure, including six One Stop Border Posts at Elegu, Mutukula, Busia, Mirama Hills, Goli, and Ntoroko, the Gulu Logistics Hub providing inland container handling and warehousing capacity, and the Uganda Electronic Single Window now integrating over 30 government agencies and contributing to a 79% reduction in import and export processing times — while partnering with the Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS) to decentralise testing laboratories to Mbale, Gulu, and Mbarara. The current strategy deepens this foundation through smart border upgrades including the climate-resilient Elegu Cross-Border Market, scaling of e-certification systems, NTB platform integration with the EAC, and inclusive trade programming.
Kampala is the capital city of Uganda

provider-org.narrative: Denmark - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Danida

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Improved Quality, Safety & Value of Traded goods (QVT)

comment.narrative: 17% further reduction in testing turnaround time was achieved across the Gulu, Mbarara, and Mbale regional laboratories, decreasing from 17 days in 2023 to less than 14 days in 2026. This improvement followed the accreditation of both Chemistry and Microbiology laboratories in the three regions by the South African National Accreditation System (SANAS) in March 2026, enhancing the quality, credibility, and efficiency of testing services. The strengthened laboratory capacity has contributed to increased uptake of certification services, with 874 permits issued and 754 companies certified, the majority of which are SMEs. These laboratories play a critical role in facilitating regional trade by providing internationally recognised testing and certification services for Uganda and neighbouring countries. For example, the laboratories were recently used to resolve a trade dispute between Uganda and South Sudan concerning aflatoxin levels in maize exports.

57% reduction in turnaround time for testing samples from 40 days on average in 2019 to 17 days on average in 2023 for testing as a result of the successful decentralisation of the testing centres in Mbale, Gulu and Mbarara.

Total cost of testing reduced by 79% on average from $ 79 on average in 2020 to $17 on average in 2023. Number of certified products increased by 122% from 130 products in 2019 to 300 products in 2023.
